meta.title: Earth Listens
meta.description: Hear NASA Earth data as deterministic sound. Built for blind and low-vision listeners, with a globe for everyone else.

banner.sample: SAMPLE DATA: not real measurements / بيانات تجريبية: ليست قياسات حقيقية
banner.nasa: Uses NASA data; not endorsed by NASA.

intro.line1: Earth is always making a sound.

story.c1title: Earth is always making a sound.
story.c1body: Before the pictures, there is a tone. A slow drone is the first sample of carbon dioxide, held quietly so you can find the room.
story.c2body: The Earth Information Center draws the planet as frames. This sample frame is labelled SAMPLE. The real frames plug in later, from the same contract.
story.c3body: A chart that only exists as colour leaves people out. The counts behind this sentence are not filled in yet. [citation needed: Basmala]
story.c4body: Where, how much, how strong, how fast, what. Each question is a separate part of the sound, and the order of the notes follows the data.
story.c5body: The sample temperature series runs from 1880 to 2025. Scrub a year. The pitch is the value. Nothing here is a forecast.
story.c6body: Start the jukebox, switch to audio-first, walk the tutorial, or guess whether a clip rose or fell.

listen.title: The jukebox
listen.summary: A text view of the planet. West is left, east is right, relative to the view centre.

quiz.title: Guess the Earth
quiz.intro: Hear a sample clip. Did the value increase, decrease, or stay the same?
quiz.explore: Could you explore this without help?
quiz.question: Did it increase, decrease, or stay the same?

sounds.title: How it sounds
sounds.lead: The Earth Sonification Language maps one data question to one part of the sound.

guide.title: Guide
guide.esl: Where is position. How much is pitch. How strong is loudness. How fast is rhythm. What is the instrument.

data.title: Data
data.lead: Every number in the app right now is SAMPLE data from a seeded formula. Real NASA and NOAA files plug in through the pipeline, without changing the engine.
data.validation: Validation plots appear here after the real data is fetched.
